title: Lower tail vanishing for complexes unbounded below
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$ be the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ of its module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects; def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible module sheaves: locally on affine opens of $X$ there is a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] on each of which the restriction has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Write $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for filtered colimits of these sheaves, computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, and $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ whose cohomology sheaves belong to $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, placed in degree zero, and fix a uniform Ext bound $d_C\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, meaning that $\Ext^r(C,N)=0$ for every $r>d_C$ and every $N\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, with Ext taken in the ambient derived category [def-pc-ext]. If $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ satisfies $H^q(L)=0$ for every $q>-d_C-1$, with no lower bound on its cohomology, then $\Hom_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(C,L)=0$.

external.place: *Milnor sequence.* Applying $\Hom(C,-)$, which takes products to products, to the defining triangle gives a long exact sequence whose relevant part is $$ \prod_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\to\Hom(C,L)\to \prod_n\Hom(C,L_n)\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_n\Hom(C,L_n), $$ i.e. $0\to\varprojlim^1_n\Hom(C,L_n[-1])\to\Hom(C,L)\to\varprojlim_n\Hom(C,L_n)\to0$.

proof.text: Use constructibleInd_extBound to extend the specified uniform Ext bound from constructible targets to each ind-constructible sheaf B. For q at most N=-d_C-1, put r=(-q).toNat. Then r>d_C and its integer cast is -q. Ext.homEquiv and singleFunctors.shiftIso identify the vanishing Ext group with Hom(C[0], singleFunctor(q) B). Zero sheaves have zero Hom as well.

proof.text: Let P be the union of the ind-constructible sheaves with the zero objects. This property is invariant under isomorphisms and contains zero. The hypothesis on L gives its cohomology in P. The pro-etale repleteness theorem, in its existing abelian-sheaf variant epi_π_app_zero_of_epi_addCommGrpCat, transfers through Mod.epiπAppZeroOfEpi to the module category. CountableAB4Star.of_epi_π_app_zero supplies exact countable products, and Grothendieckness supplies K-injective resolutions.

proof.text: Apply the abstract strict-tail devissage to all complexes in P supported in degrees at most N-1. It proves Hom(C[0],M)=0 for such M using bounded cohomological induction and the existing generic left-completeness/Milnor triangle. This is a direct invocation of the complete source-library proof, not a new unproved reduction.

proof.text: Take the distinguished truncation triangle tau_lt(N)L -> L -> tau_ge(N)L. The first term has upper bound N-1, so step 3 kills its Hom. The last is supported in the single degree N because L has upper bound N; its cohomology is in P, and the single-degree case of the same source-library bounded devissage kills its Hom by step 1. Representable Hom exactness factors any map C[0] -> L through the first term and makes it zero. This proves Subsingleton for both coefficient choices without changing the endpoint or adding geometric assumptions.

This retains bounded devissage and Postnikov convergence without reproving eventual-transition recursion.
